title: Generic quasi-separatedness of a finite type morphism
statement: Let $h:Z\to T$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with $T$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. There is a nonempty open subscheme $W\subseteq T$ such that $h^{-1}(W)\to W$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Neither $T$ nor $Z$ is assumed Noetherian, and $h$ is not assumed separated or quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 052A, proposition-generic-flatness, quasi-separatedness conclusion in the last paragraph of its proof

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$. By [def-pc-integral-scheme], $A$ is a domain. The finite-affine-cover characterization of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives a finite cover $h^{-1}(V)=\bigcup_{i=1}^n Z_i$, where $Z_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and each $B_i$ is a finite type $A$-algebra. By the Zariski topology on [def-weil-affine-spectrum], closed subsets are zero loci of ideals. For each ordered pair choose an ideal $I_{ij}\subseteq B_i$ defining the closed subset $Z_i\setminus(Z_i\cap Z_j)$, and put $M_{ij}=B_i/I_{ij}$. This is a finite $B_i$-module, generated by the class of $1$; no finite generation of $I_{ij}$ is asserted. If the source over $V$ is empty, the cover and the pairs are empty.

Apply [lem-pur-generic-finite-module-presentation] to each cyclic quotient B_i/I_ij. Mathlib Submodule.toLocalizedQuotient' and IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv identify its module of fractions with the quotient of the localized ring by the extended ideal; extend the linear equivalence to localized scalars. Module.support_of_algebra and Ideal.mk_ker identify its support with the zero locus of that ideal. By [lem-pur-finitely-presented-support-complement] the complement is compact in the localized spectrum. Its image in Spec B_i is the original intersection restricted to D(a_ij), by localization_away_comap_range. Compactness persists at every base element divisible by a_ij: the further restriction is the intersection with another compact basic open in the quasi-separated spectrum. Take the finite product a of the a_ij (the empty product is 1). The domain property implies a is nonzero and hence D(a) is nonempty. Each a_ij divides a, so every chart intersection is compact on this one shrinking.

Transfer the spectrum compactness computation to each affine chart by its canonical isoSpec homeomorphism and HasRingHomProperty.iff_of_isAffine for finite type. The preimage of D(a) in each chart is the basic open defined by the image of a; [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], as used by Mathlib IsAffineOpen.ι_basicOpen_preimage, makes the restricted charts affine. Pull back the finite chart cover to the restricted source. The image of each chart-complement computation is exactly the image of the corresponding intersection in this restricted source; write the witnesses explicitly and transfer compactness through the source inclusion, an open embedding.

Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion], implemented by Scheme.quasiSeparatedSpace_of_isOpenCover, to the restricted affine cover and its compact intersections. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], implemented by QuasiSeparated.of_quasiSeparatedSpace, makes the restricted morphism quasi-separated. For a general integral base choose a nonempty affine open, whose scheme remains integral, apply the affine-base construction to the restricted morphism, and take the image of the resulting nonempty open in the original base. Transfer quasi-separatedness along morphismRestrictRestrict using the isomorphism-invariance of the morphism property. All finite products and covers include the empty-source case.
